done_when: forge test --pytest runs the whole suite for a pyproject.toml change only when its dependency or pytest settings change, and only related tests otherwise; every uv command Forge runs uses the lockfile without rewriting it, so no Forge command leaves uv.lock changed; one command test per case; new and earlier-adopted client repos get it, with a command test for each

findings.body: The dependency projection omits entire dependency-bearing namespaces. Changing `[tool.tox.env_run_base] deps` or a named tox environment's `deps` leaves both snapshots equal, so Forge runs related tests—or returns success without testing at lines 297–299—instead of the full suite. The same omission affects Flit's `tool.flit.metadata.requires`, `requires-extra` and `requires-python`, and Rye's `tool.rye.dev-dependencies`, `excluded-dependencies` and dependency sources. New evidence beyond the previous uv/Hatch ruling: these are documented dependency inputs in [tox's native TOML configuration](https://tox.wiki/en/4.64.2/reference/config.html#deps), [Flit's supported older metadata format](https://flit.pypa.io/en/3.12.0/pyproject_toml.html#old-style-metadata), and [Rye's project configuration](https://rye.astral.sh/guide/pyproject/). The command regression table contains none of these namespaces, so every listed proof can pass while dependency edits still skip full execution. Include these dependency inputs and extend the existing command-level table.

stop.reason: Owner: fail closed with a safe list. Any pyproject.toml change runs the full suite unless every changed line sits in a short list of known-harmless sections (packaged-file build settings, project version and description); no dependency hunting

why: Any pyproject.toml change makes forge test --pytest run the whole suite locally (30+ minutes holding the test slot), and uv run rewrites uv.lock back to an old cached version in older worktrees, leaving stray changes that block closes and cleanup
